messages:
maria: Heads-up — I'm starting a small experiment for an automated cordon/soft-evict flow driven by composite GPU health signals (ECC + Xid + resets). This is probe-only initially (no mass evacs).

josh: Nice. What exactly counts as a trigger? we already have the 5-min Xid detector.

maria: Composite trigger: (ecc_error_rate > 0.6 && xid_error_rate > 0.2) OR card_reset_count >= 2 in 30m. But probe mode will just cordon + run a quick workload smoke. If probe fails, escalate to soft-drain.

kai: Can you paste the cordon command you're using? need to review k8s vs slurm paths.

maria: K8s path (probe):
```bash
# cordon only, no eviction
kubectl cordon node/${NODE} 
# then run a single low-q pod on that node as a canary
kubectl run gpu-probe --image=redwood/gpu-smoke:latest --requests='nvidia.com/gpu=1' --overrides='\{"spec\":\{"nodeName\":\"${NODE}\"\}}' --restart=Never
```

ana: For Slurm nodes we should avoid kill/requeue for running high-priority jobs. Proposal: probe via srun --nodelist=$NODE --gres=gpu:1 --time=00:05:00 and only set NodeState=POWER_SAVE if probe fails.

ana: slurm snippet:
```bash
# quick probe job that won't preempt high-prio
srun --nodelist=$NODE --gres=gpu:1 --pty /bin/true || scontrol update NodeName=$NODE State=DRAIN Reason="gpu-probe-fail"
```

josh: What about safelist/whitelist? we must prevent auto-cordon on nodes pinned for enterprise reserved capacity.

maria: Agreed. We'll maintain a safelist stored in config service (env tag: gpu_autodrain_safelist) and a circuit-breaker that prevents >10% of a region's GPU pool from being quarantined. If circuit trips, we auto-backout (un-cordon any probe-marked nodes).

maria: Circuit-breaker pseudocode:
```py
# pseudo
if quarantined_in_region / total_region_gpus > 0.1:
    backout_probes()
    notify(#infra-oncall)
```

devops: Rolling feature flag: gpu-autodrain.experimental=true in eu-west1 canary (1 node / AZ) for 24h. Will monitor token-level latency and core SLO.

infra-ci: preflight: gpu-probe smoke image built: sha256:abcd1234. Integration test: gpu-probe -> PASS.

sre-bot: Monitoring alert created: GPU_AUTODRAIN_PROBE_FAILURES (severity: low). Alert window: 30m.

josh: How do we detect false positives? ECC bursts sometimes correlate with firmware updates and then stop. We should require a stable signal across 3 samples with linear growth, not a single spike.

maria: Yes — sample spacing is 10m. We require 3/3 consecutive windows or (reset_count >=2) immediate probe. That cuts false positives.

kai: What about KV cache invalidation for long-running chat sessions? Evicting nodes mid-ttl can hit tail-latency. Any plan to tag sessions and migrate?

maria: For now probe-only avoids major disruption. For soft-drain we will attempt graceful KV cache export via agent and advertise fallback routing to same-region spare pool. More advanced session-migration is next phase.

ana: One more: add a manual override label for scheduled maint windows so autosystem ignores nodes we expect to service. label: gpu.autodrain/ignore=true

maria: Agreed. I'll open a PR with config schema, safelist integration, and the backout circuit logic. Plan: canary in eu-west1 for 24h, then expand to us-west with tighter backoff.

josh: :eyes: please add runbook steps for oncall: how to force uncordon, how to mark safelist nodes, and how to flip the feature flag.

infra-ci: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821 (gpu-autodrain-probe-and-safelist). CI: 7/7 green.

maria: Thanks — I'll post the rollout doc in #eng-runtime and schedule a quick sync with SRE + Slurm owners tomorrow. :thumbsup:
